critiques.issue: Each step was kept as 'accuracy unchanged within noise', but the salt-0 means fall every time: 0.7556 → 0.7539 → 0.7535 → 0.7533 → 0.7531. Each kept run passed the 0.753 bar on one draw. Only E025 and E033 got salt-1 companions (0.7527 and 0.7518). The 2-salt estimate of the incumbent, 0.7525, is below the local bar. With the expected value at the bar, every further time cut has roughly a 50% chance of passing by noise alone. Keeps are now selecting lucky trajectories, which is the winner's-curse ratchet that H4 warns about.
critiques.suggestion: Before any time cut is kept, require a 2-salt mean ≥ 0.753, or a salt-0 result ≥ 0.755. Stop cutting time until a change that adds margin passes with 2 salts. Treat E029 and E030 as unreplicated and give them salt-1 runs, or at least pool them, before claiming their 'no accuracy cost'.

critiques.issue: This is the most decision-relevant open test and it has never been run. E034 has since put the incumbent's expected accuracy at about 0.7525. All the noise estimates come from 6 draws or fewer. They disagree by 5x: per-seed std was about 0.40 pp on E025/E027 and about 0.08 pp on E033/E034, so the inconclusive band used in verdicts is not pinned down.
critiques.suggestion: Run the E033 recipe on dev seeds 3-12, outside the official command. That gives the expected accuracy and the per-seed std. Then decide whether a lower variance after freezing is real, and set one inconclusive band for all later verdicts.

critiques.target: H1.8 / 'epochs no longer buy margin' (E032, E036 post-mortems)
critiques.issue: The plateau conclusion rests on two single-salt runs on different bases. E032 ran on E025, before the detach and the 20 px stage. E036 ran on E030. Both changes are confounded with schedule coupling. Everything is defined over total steps: the triangle peak, the Lookahead alpha ramp and the whitening-bias epochs all move. Each delta is about 1 SE or less. H1.8 is still 'open' at 0.55 and still says 'steeply under-trained', with E036- attached. That matches neither reading. A true plateau near 75% at about 10 epochs would also be surprising for this architecture class on CIFAR-100.
critiques.suggestion: Run one large, clean test: +1.5 to 2 full-res epochs with the schedule anchors fixed in absolute steps (warmup length, Lookahead ramp and bias window unchanged), with 2 salts. If accuracy rises by ≥0.5 pp, epochs remain a margin lever and E036 was a schedule-coupling artifact. Rewrite H1.8 to match whichever result comes back.

critiques.target: Missing Lvl1: accuracy ceiling from capacity/regularization
critiques.issue: The current Lvl1s do not explain why accuracy stays near 0.753 whatever is changed: more epochs (E032, E036), Muon lr ×1.25 (E028), ls by resolution (E026), EMA (E019). H1 assumes steps buy accuracy and H2 is only about speed. No Lvl1 says that the recipe's accuracy is capped by model capacity or the regularization balance at this resolution ladder.
critiques.suggestion: Add a Lvl1 along these lines: 'margin is capacity/regularization-limited'. Give it falsifiable children: group-2/3 width at equal epochs on the current frozen-block recipe (deep layers are almost free per E004/E008 timing), an extra conv in group 3, and ls 0.4. Check each with 2 salts.

critiques.issue: The claim that 'under Muon, the width bonus is ≤0.2 pp' comes from one run. That run (E008) changed width and cut 0.5 epoch at the same time, at batch 2000, before resizing, CUDA graphs or block freezing. The evidence tokens E009+ and E010+ come from group-1 cuts and do not bear on the group-3 width claim.
critiques.suggestion: Remove E009 and E010 from H1.5. Test width at equal epochs (group 3 at 768, or group 2 at 448-512) on E033 with 2 salts. It is the cheapest untested margin lever, because width at low resolution costs about 6-7% per step.

critiques.issue: Only the lr was raised (×1.25, E028). The ×0.8 arm in the H1.7.6 prediction was never run, and momentum has never been varied, although the statement claims 'a small lr/momentum sweep'. Weight decay is the SGD-era 0.012 and its interaction with Muon's per-step renorm has never been examined. The flat lr response (E028) is itself surprising. With per-step weight renorm, lr should set the angular step size. Flatness points to Lookahead or the renorm damping lr, not to lr being optimal.
critiques.suggestion: Run momentum {0.6, 0.75} and lr ×0.8 on E033, with 2 salts each. Separately, log the per-layer angular update size at lr 0.205 vs 0.256 to test whether Lookahead or renorm is cancelling the lr change.

critiques.issue: Two components were removed in one run (-0.52 pp), and the post-mortem says the split was never done. It is unknown which component does the work. The LR floor (H1.7.5) was also retired without a test.
critiques.suggestion: If margin is the bottleneck, test the triangle with Lookahead's final sync replaced by a different end LR (5% of peak, H1.7.5), and test Lookahead with a shorter warmup. These are time-neutral changes that could add margin.

critiques.issue: The statement predicts 3→2 NS steps with AOL. That is exactly what E024 tested, and it supported the prediction. E035 tested 2→1, which is a different prediction. Marking H2.5.2 refuted on E035- misstates the record. The renorm-every-k part has never been tested.
critiques.suggestion: Attach E024+ to H2.5.2 and record E035 as refuting a new Lvl3 ('1 NS step suffices'). Keep the renorm-every-k arm open, since it saves time without cutting steps, which E031 and E035 show is dangerous under Muon.

critiques.issue: H2.3.1 is 'open' although its own verdict is supports (E025+). H1.1.2 is 'refuted' with E002+ and a 'supports' verdict. H2.3 lists E026~, a regularization test, as resizing evidence. H2.4 omits E029+. H4's text ('23 runs') is stale. H3 is still framed as a lever when prepare is about 1% of time.
critiques.suggestion: Reconcile status with the verdicts. Close H3 as exhausted. Update H4's text to the current incumbent and the E034 estimate.

critiques.target: H2.4 mechanism ('low conv efficiency at small channel counts')
critiques.issue: The successes (E029, E033) show that removing high-res backward work is free. They do not test the stated cause. H2.4.1 showed non-conv kernels are about 23% of fwd+bwd, which is not negligible, yet no fusion or BN-folding idea has been tried. Under E033, the frozen 32 px block still runs BN in train mode. It could be folded into the conv as a fixed affine.
critiques.suggestion: Split H2.4 into a work-removal Lvl2 and a kernel-efficiency Lvl2. Add Lvl3s: (a) in the 32 px phase, fold the frozen block's BN into its conv, or put that BN in eval mode, with 2 salts since the running stats change; (b) swap GELU for ReLU at 32x32 and 16x16, with timing and 2 salts.

critiques.issue: This is the most productive recent line: -2.6% and -3.9% with no measured accuracy loss. Only one extension has been tried. E037 notes that the 28 px phase keeps conv1 trainable. Freezing the block in the 28 px phase, or stopping backward through all of group 1 in the final epoch, has not been tried.
critiques.suggestion: Add a Lvl3 under H2.4: freeze group-1 conv1 in the 28 px phase too, and/or detach all of group 1 for the last 1-2 epochs. Pair it with a margin-adding change, because the base is at the bar.

critiques.target: Untested Lvl3s inherited from the start (H1.2.1, H1.3.2, H2.4.3, H1.6.2)
critiques.issue: Alternating flip vs random flip and Cutout were never tested. Both are hypotheses about free accuracy, which is what the loop now needs. H2.4.3 (group-1 width 112) predates E033's freezing and is probably moot. H1.6.2 has a weak prior after E013 (-0.73 pp).
critiques.suggestion: Prioritize H1.2.1. Flipping a random-vs-alternating flag tests whether alternating is helping or hurting on CIFAR-100. Retire H1.6.2 and either re-scope H2.4.3 to the frozen regime or retire it.

critiques.target: E036 surprise (an extra 20 px epoch lowered accuracy)
critiques.issue: Besides noise, the likely mechanisms are concrete and checkable. The fixed 23% warmup moves the peak LR. The whitening-bias window, fixed at 'the low-res phase', changes length. The Lookahead alpha ramp stretches. Together with E031 (fewer early steps → -0.44 pp) and E022 (more steps → +0.09), the evidence points to step count and placement relative to the schedule as the variable, not epochs. No hypothesis states this.
critiques.suggestion: Add a Lvl2 under H1: 'accuracy depends on optimizer steps at peak and decay LR, not on epochs or pixels'. Test it by adding low-res steps while holding the absolute warmup and decay step counts fixed.

critiques.target: H5 (PCIe transfer) and recent small wins
critiques.issue: Several kept wins are 1.8-3% (E024, E025, E029, E030). H5 says sub-2% wins tied to scheduling may not transfer. Most of these remove work (pixels, backward passes), so they should transfer. E024's AOL+NS change is partly an overhead cut, and nothing checks it beyond its local 2% win.
critiques.suggestion: When ranking candidates with local deltas under 2%, prefer the ones that remove work, as H5.1 recommends. Note that E024's gain is the only overhead-type cut in the current stack that has not been checked on the PCIe judge.

structured_output.summary: The loop stopped finding real gains at about E024. Since then every kept change cut time, and each was accepted on one 3-seed draw that cleared 0.753 by 0.03-0.09 pp, while the salt-0 means fell monotonically. The 2-salt estimate of the incumbent is 0.7525, below the local bar, so future keeps are close to coin flips. The noise model rests on 6 or fewer draws, and its per-seed std estimates disagree by 5x (0.08 vs 0.40 pp). H4.3, the dev-seed test that would settle this, has never been run. The claim that 'epochs no longer help' rests on two confounded single-salt runs on different bases. No Lvl1 explains the apparent ceiling near 75.3% across epochs, lr, ls and EMA: neither capacity/regularization limits nor schedule coupling of step placement is covered. Cheap margin levers remain untested: group-2/3 width at equal epochs, Muon momentum, lr ×0.8, splitting the Lookahead/triangle change, alternating vs random flip, and ls 0.4. The productive FreezeOut/work-removal line (E029, E033) has room to extend, and BN folding in frozen blocks is unexplored. Several evidence attributions and statuses are wrong: H2.5.2 vs E024/E035, H1.5 vs E009/E010, H2.3.1 still open, and H1.1.2's status. Recommended order: (1) dev-seed and 2-salt calibration of E033; (2) 2-salt tests of changes that add margin (width, momentum, flip, a large epoch step with schedule anchors fixed); (3) only then more freeze or fold time cuts, paired with the gained margin.
